RAW_T1_READY.description: A raw T1-weighted image is present but no VBM preprocessing has started. The pipeline is at the very beginning.
RAW_T1_READY.next_step: Run tissue segmentation using SPM Unified Segmentation or CAT12.
RAW_T1_READY.why_needed: Segmentation is the foundation of the whole VBM pipeline. Every downstream file is derived from the tissue probability maps it produces, so errors here propagate through every subsequent step.
expected_outputs: y_*.nii (forward deformation field to MNI space)
qc_risks: Poor input contrast from motion or low SNR causes noisy tissue maps
A strong uncorrected bias field can misclassify entire brain regions
Pediatric, elderly, or pathological brains deviate from the adult template priors SPM uses
Left-right flips in the header go undetected and corrupt all downstream results

SEGMENTATION_COMPLETED.description: Tissue segmentation is done. Gray matter, white matter, and CSF probability maps exist. No normalization has happened yet.
SEGMENTATION_COMPLETED.next_step: For SPM-DARTEL: run DARTEL import to rigidly align tissue maps. For CAT12: proceed directly to normalization.
SEGMENTATION_COMPLETED.why_needed: The tissue maps are still in each subject's native space. Before voxel-by-voxel comparison across subjects is possible, they need to be aligned to a common space, which is what normalization accomplishes.
expected_outputs: rc1*.nii, rc2*.nii (DARTEL import) or wc1*.nii, wp1*.nii (direct CAT12 normalization)
qc_risks: Overlay tissue maps on the original T1 to confirm they sit in the right anatomical regions before proceeding
A subject with a visibly poor segmentation should be reprocessed or excluded before DARTEL, since a bad segmentation pulls the group template toward it

DARTEL_INPUT_READY.description: DARTEL import is done. Rigidly aligned tissue maps (rc1, rc2) exist and are ready for the iterative DARTEL alignment step.
DARTEL_INPUT_READY.next_step: Run DARTEL alignment across all subjects to build a study-specific group template and compute each subject's flow field.
DARTEL_INPUT_READY.why_needed: DARTEL builds a template from your actual subjects rather than warping to a generic adult atlas. This study-specific template captures the shape characteristics of your group and produces more accurate warps, especially for atypical populations.
qc_risks: DARTEL needs at least 20 subjects to produce a stable template -- smaller studies need a different approach
If any subject's tissue maps looked suspicious at the segmentation QC step, fix or exclude them before running DARTEL

DARTEL_COMPLETED.description: DARTEL alignment is done. Subject-specific flow fields (u_rc1) and iterative group templates (Template_0 through Template_6) exist.
DARTEL_COMPLETED.next_step: Run normalization to warp each subject's tissue maps into MNI standard space using their flow field.
DARTEL_COMPLETED.why_needed: The flow fields computed by DARTEL encode how each subject's brain shape differs from the group template. Normalization applies these flow fields to bring all subjects into a common MNI coordinate system where voxel-by-voxel comparison is meaningful.
expected_outputs: wc1*.nii or wp1*.nii (warped gray matter in MNI space)
wc2*.nii or wp2*.nii (warped white matter in MNI space)
mwc1*.nii or mwp1*.nii (modulated warped gray matter, volume-preserving)
qc_risks: Check Template_6.nii -- it should look like a blurry but clearly recognizable brain
Any subject whose flow field produces a visibly distorted warped image should be investigated for upstream segmentation problems
Confirm the final template was built from the expected number of subjects

NORMALIZATION_COMPLETED.description: Normalization is done. Warped and modulated tissue maps in MNI space exist. Smoothing has not been run yet.
prerequisite_files: mwc1*.nii or mwp1*.nii (modulated warped gray matter)
NORMALIZATION_COMPLETED.next_step: Run Gaussian smoothing on the modulated warped gray matter maps.
NORMALIZATION_COMPLETED.why_needed: Even after normalization, small residual misalignments remain between subjects. Smoothing blurs the data so each voxel reflects a neighborhood average, which makes comparisons more robust and satisfies the smoothness assumptions required for the statistical corrections applied in the final analysis.
expected_outputs: smwc1*.nii or smwp1*.nii (smoothed modulated warped gray matter -- final input to statistics)
smwc2*.nii or smwp2*.nii (smoothed modulated warped white matter)
qc_risks: Overlay warped maps on the MNI template and verify that major landmarks align across subjects before smoothing
Check the modulated maps for extreme intensity values that might indicate a bad warp

SMOOTHING_COMPLETED.description: Smoothing is done and final VBM input files exist, but not all earlier pipeline files have been verified in this folder.
prerequisite_files: smwc1*.nii or smwp1*.nii (smoothed modulated warped gray matter)
SMOOTHING_COMPLETED.next_step: Verify earlier-stage files are present, then proceed to second-level statistical analysis.
SMOOTHING_COMPLETED.why_needed: Having the smoothed files without confirming the full pipeline history means it is harder to trace and fix any problems that appear in the statistical results.
expected_outputs: SPM.mat, beta_*.nii, spmT_*.nii (from second-level GLM analysis)
qc_risks: Confirm segmentation and normalization files are also present before running statistics
Do a final visual check comparing smwc1 files across subjects -- obvious outliers at this stage should be excluded

VBM_READY_FOR_STATISTICS.description: The full preprocessing pipeline is complete and all prerequisite files have been verified. This folder is ready for second-level statistical analysis.
VBM_READY_FOR_STATISTICS.next_step: Run second-level GLM analysis in SPM using all subjects' smwc1 or smwp1 files.
VBM_READY_FOR_STATISTICS.why_needed: The preprocessed maps from all subjects need to be fed into a voxel-wise statistical model that can identify where gray matter volume differs between groups or correlates with a variable of interest, while controlling for confounds like age, sex, and head size.
expected_outputs: SPM.mat (design matrix, contrasts, and results object)
Thresholded cluster maps after FWE or FDR correction
qc_risks: Always include total intracranial volume (TIV) as a covariate to control for head size
Use FWE or FDR correction -- uncorrected results are not publishable in structural MRI analysis
Check residual variance maps after fitting the GLM for patches of unusually high or low variance

INCOMPLETE_OR_ERROR.description: Files are present in the folder but the pipeline state does not make logical sense. Later-stage files exist without the earlier-stage files that should have produced them.
INCOMPLETE_OR_ERROR.next_step: Investigate which files are missing, check whether earlier preprocessing outputs were accidentally deleted or moved, and rerun the missing steps if necessary.
INCOMPLETE_OR_ERROR.why_needed: A logically inconsistent folder state means the pipeline history cannot be reconstructed. Running further steps on top of incomplete inputs will produce results that cannot be trusted.
qc_risks: Do not proceed with any further processing until the inconsistency is understood
Check whether files were moved to a different folder rather than deleted
If the earlier steps need to be rerun, make sure the original T1 input is still available
